requiredStrings: const doc = new jsPDF(layout.orientation, layout.units, layout.page);
GeoMoose uses jsPDF to perform client-side generation of PDF printouts.
A print layout is comprised of a label, orientation, page size, unit
``image`` - Add an image to the map.

knownDifferences: GeoMoose's 3.15.2 print-layout guide says there are four built-in templates, while the exact source exports five. The comparison and converter follow the exact exported source inventory and retain the documentation mismatch as upstream evidence.

OpenGeo converts GeoMoose page geometry into its normalized 1000 by 1000 positioned-page coordinate space and retains the source paper size and orientation as print options; rounding is bounded but physical coordinate identity is not claimed.
GeoMoose rect and ellipse drawing instructions have no OpenGeo print-layout 1.1 frame and are omitted with one explicit source-element outcome apiece; no visual approximation is claimed.

GeoMoose font family, face, exact point size, and color map to bounded semantic OpenGeo text styles. The four default title/date tokens are resolved from explicit inputs; unknown tokens remain literal and are reported.

GeoMoose live legend images become the exact legend sealed with the OpenGeo map snapshot. Inline image bytes are never read; an image converts only when the caller supplies an explicit sealed OpenGeo content-block binding and dimensions.

GeoMoose's print resolution, include-selection option, portal-configured scale line, and jsPDF GeoArea extent live outside the layout object and are recorded as four external-context losses rather than silently converted.

This exact-source local comparison imports configuration but does not execute jsPDF, compare rendered PDF/PNG pixels, validate touch or operating-system assistive technology, deploy resources, or change fixed inactive cost.
